teams.heading: Jake White hails Fiji as 'Harlem Globetrotters', targets maul and scrum fixes
teams.body: After Friday's 23-21 defeat to Italy at Twickenham, the head coach said one of Fiji's tries was probably the best of the tournament, with prop forwards passing out of the back of their hands. His verdict was simple: “they are the Harlem Globetrotters of rugby.” His priorities are more basic. Stopping mauls remains a work in progress, and he wants a scrum that does not give penalties away before adding the bells and whistles. White predicted Fiji will be much better by next year's World Cup.

lead.why: Fresh, Fiji-centred coach verdict from Jake White on his side's identity and fixes, distinct from the result and pundit stories already run.

teams.heading: Coles and Pollock sin-binned as All Blacks beat England 26-8 at Twickenham
teams.body: Saturday's Nations Championship play-off went the way of Dave Rennie's side a week after England's 37-12 rout, with Richie Mo'unga landing four penalties and two conversions. Borthwick's side needed 12 entries to the 22 for a single try, Jamie George finishing a maul, while yellow cards for Alex Coles — a head-high tackle on 33 minutes — and Henry Pollock kept Mo'unga's boot busy. On 60 minutes Twickenham booed its own team after an aimless Marcus Smith kick found the New Zealand backfield.

lead.why: England's defeat in Saturday's play-off is the material new development on the All Blacks rematch, and the reader has not yet seen it.

teams.heading: Fabien Galthié starts all-Bordeaux front row of Poirot, Lamothe and Falatea
teams.body: The Bordeaux-Bègles trio get the nod for today's Nations Championship final against South Africa at Twickenham, with Jean-Baptiste Gros and Peato Mauvaka held back for the last half-hour. Planet Rugby reads it as a trio picked to fight the Springboks on the floor as much as in the scrum. It is a pointed call: in Paris a fortnight ago, France led 21-7 before the Bok scrum took over, and they conceded 14 penalties and three yellow cards in hanging on to win 21-19.

teams.heading: Ireland made 215 tackles beating Australia; Nick Timoney hails instant rebound
teams.body: Friday's 38-14 win over Australia at Allianz Stadium was earned largely without the ball. The Wallabies had more than 90% possession before Jeremy Williams burrowed over for a 7-0 lead, and made only 129 tackles all night. Robbie Henshaw's try had it level within minutes, though Timoney conceded: "It didn't come all that naturally." Both sides managed 11 entries to the 22; Ireland turned theirs into five tries and a penalty, the Wallabies into two.

lead.why: Ireland's defensive workload against Australia is a fresh angle on the win, with Timoney's own account, and avoids the Prendergast and McNabney stories already run.

teams.heading: Tommaso Menoncello needs shoulder surgery and looks set to miss Six Nations
teams.body: The Toulouse centre broke down in training with a recurrence of the acromioclavicular sprain he suffered against Exeter in the Champions Cup in mid-October. A month and a half of conservative treatment had brought him back to training, seemingly close to a return, before the shoulder gave way. OnRugby puts the lay-off at three to four months. Even at the short end he would return in late February or early March without match minutes, too late, the outlet reckons, to risk for the Six Nations' closing rounds.

lead.why: A fresh injury to a first-choice Italy centre threatens his Six Nations, and it is the only new event in the pack about the men's XV.

teams.heading: Rory Darge returns from injury to captain Townsend's 11-change Scotland side
teams.body: Darge leads a side in which only Darcy Graham, Rory Hutchinson, Jamie Dobie and Jonny Gray survive from the 67-5 rout of Japan, with Finn Russell back at fly-half for Sunday's seventh-place final against Argentina at Twickenham. With the squad's No. 8s injured, Gregor Townsend turns to Magnus Bradbury: "I'm sure he knows it's a big opportunity for him ahead of the Six Nations." Townsend also revealed he considered replacement hooker Seb Stephen at No. 8 before deciding against it this weekend.

teams.heading: Josh Adams and Jac Morgan score twice as Wales beat Japan 40-10
teams.body: Saturday's ninth-place play-off at a rain-soaked Twickenham was won through the boot, with Sam Costelow's cross-field kick sending Adams over for the opener. Eddie James's chip later gave Adams a second. Reuben Morgan-Williams scored on his first Wales start and Blair Murray crossed before the break. Morgan, on as a replacement, finished a driving maul and then a tap-penalty move in the second half. With Ellis Mee in for the ill Louis Rees-Zammit, Wales won on 37 per cent of the ball, kicking 1,216 metres to Japan's 511.

teams.heading: Pumas' Rugby Championship partners SANZAAR fight World Rugby over 2030 relegation
teams.body: SANZAAR has joined the Six Nations in a fresh push to strip relegation from the 2030 Nations Championship, putting Argentina's southern partners in a new fight with the governing body. World Rugby refused to back down this month, WalesOnline reported, as 'cataclysmic' relegation fears were realised. The looming threat was reported as the inaugural tournament reached its decisive stage, with the Pumas bound for the seventh-place final against Scotland. Nothing closes until World Rugby and the Tier 1 unions formally agree the 2030 structure, and no deal has been reported.

teams.heading: Max Jorgensen fails HIA after 29 minutes of Wallabies' Ireland defeat
teams.body: The wing failed his HIA and went off after 29 minutes of Friday's 38-14 fifth-place play-off loss to Ireland at Allianz Stadium, following an aerial collision. Until then he had been strong in the air and a willing chaser. His exit forced a backline reshuffle that brought on Kurtley Beale, who Planet Rugby says got in Carter Gordon's way. The outlet allowed that the reshuffle didn't help, but still called Australia the architects of their own demise.

teams.heading: Eddie Jones faces JRFU review after winless autumn closes with Wales defeat
teams.body: Japan Rugby Football Union president Masato Tsuchida has confirmed the campaign will be reviewed, according to reports in Japan. It ended with Saturday's 40-10 defeat by Wales at Twickenham: four losses from four and 213 points conceded. Tsuchida indicated last weekend that Jones was likely to stay, pointing to the difficulty of finding a replacement. Jones's mitigation is an injury list that forced regular flanker Tiennan Costley to start on the wing against Wales.

lead.why: Jones's future going under formal review is the Japan story a fan would text about, ahead of a result that only rounds it off.

teams.heading: Richie Mo'unga kicks 16 points as All Blacks beat England 26-8
teams.body: Mo'unga was flawless off the tee in Saturday's Nations Championship finals-weekend meeting at Twickenham. He kicked four penalties and two conversions as the All Blacks reversed last week's 37-12 defeat at the same ground. No. 8 Wallace Sititi powered over for the opening try, and replacement scrumhalf Cam Roigard bounced off Jack van Poortvliet for the second, earning man of the match. England had Alex Coles and Henry Pollock sin-binned, and Jordie Barrett's first outing as captain ended in victory.

lead.why: Saturday's result is the fresh New Zealand event, and this report carries the fullest scoring detail.

teams.heading: Banned Rassie Erasmus unmutes himself for Nations Championship final watchalong
teams.body: Serving a six-match ban, Erasmus muted himself during last week's watchalong of the Ireland Test in Dublin, speaking only briefly before kick-off and at half-time. Sunday's final against France will be different. "Thanks for being there with me last week, this time my sound is on, right through the game," he posted on X, promising to chat before kick-off, at the break and after the final whistle. He says almost 200,000 fans have signed up — Twickenham holds 82,000.

lead.why: A fresh decision by the banned Bok coach for the final. The back-row reshuffle and the ban fallout have already run.
